segments.he: רבינו ז"ל אמר מקנא אני את ר' יוסקא (היינו לעניין פשיטות שקורין פראסטאק בלי חכמות "ערינסט") זה הר' יוסקא הי' איש פשוט מאד והי' לו סידור עב מהסידורים הישנים שכתוב כל התחנות והיוצרות והי' לוקח זה הסידור לביהכנ"ס והי' אומרו כולו מתחלה ועד סוף ולא הי' מחסר כלום מר"ה ופורים והגדה וכו' הכל כאשר לכל אמר בלי הבנה להבדיל. וזה הי' כ"כ בפשיטות ובתמימות).
segments.en: Reb Mikhel of Tulchin told that he knew relatives of Reb Yosil the Silent. This Reb Yosil was a companion of the holy Tzaddik Reb Levi Yitzchak of Berdichev and was very great. His custom was to say witty things [aglakh vertlakh]. Once he argued with the Tzaddik of Berdichev about a pshat in the Gemara. The Tzaddik of Berdichev said: "This is how it is studied up in Heaven in the firmament." Reb Yosil replied with a witticism: "And in Heaven — can they not make a mistake?" "In Hime'l ken men den kayn ta'us nit hobn?" The Tzaddik of Berdichev was deeply moved and said with great arousal: "Yosil — see what your jesting has brought you to!" "Yosil, di holst dikh nokh in vertlekh — zey tsi vos di vertlekh hobn dikh gebrakht!" These words penetrated deeply. From that day he resolved not only to stop jesting — but to be completely silent and not speak at all. He fulfilled this with utter self-sacrifice — for his very life-force had been the saying of witty things. When he denied himself from this, his very limbs dried up from the affliction. His relative told Reb Mikhel that when he saw him in the bathhouse he was so dried up and thin one could almost see his inner organs. His relative said: "Reb Yosil — you have afflicted yourself enough." He replied with great arousal: "Der guf iz azoy mugoshem — loz im nor op eyn tog — iz er shoyn der eygenem vos er iz geven!" [The body is so coarse — leave it alone just one day and it already returns to what it was!]
